correctness.rationale: Over C, the smooth projective general-pencil variety has isolated fixed points for the action in Fonarev–Kuznetsov. By Brosnan's integral theorem, each point contributes an integral Tate motive with twist equal to its attracting-cell dimension in the stated convention. The comparison Grassmannian has a Schubert paving (equivalently the BB cells of a generic diagonal one-parameter subgroup). Theorem 1.1 supplies exactly the equality of each multiplicity needed to obtain a noncanonical isomorphism. Independently, the same finite decomposition into locally closed affine spaces gives equality by the scissor relation. Dimensions are both 2k(n+1−k); the extreme k=1 gives projective space and k=n+1 has one zero-dimensional cell. No product-preserving identification is proved or asserted.
residual_risks: The conclusion concerns Chow motives over C in Brosnan's convention, not the multiplicative structure of either ring.
